pride_data.title: Secretome profile of living constructs assembled from cell-to-cell crosslinking of human adipose tissue-derived mesenchymal stromal cells
pride_data.projectDescription: We report proteomic data from living constructs assembled entirely from human cells covalently tethered via interfacial bridges with a glycosaminoglycan. Here, bioorthogonal azide groups are installed in cell surface glycoproteins via metabolic glycoengineering, allowing for catalyst-free click-chemistry coupling with a complementary hyaluronan biopolymer. This cell-to-cell tethering strategy enables the use of human cells as active crosslinkers and main building blocks of macroscale, tissue-dense living materials. In light of this, we explore the secretome profile of these constructs following a maturation period of 3 days. Bioinformatic analysis and matrisome annotation revealed the presence of a wide range of proteins related to extracellular matrix organization, assembly and remodeling, as well as proteins involved in cell signaling and migration. These findings highlight the potential of this cell-to-cell tethering strategy for creating nascent living tissue mimetics that can be explored in tissue engineering and regenerative medicine endeavors.
pride_data.sampleProcessingProtocol: Sample harvesting Upon a 3-day maturation period, the secretome of disc-shaped living materials comprised by human adipose tissue-derived mesenchymal stromal cells (Ø = 6 mm × 1.5 mm height, n = 5) was evaluated. Briefly, following maturation, these constructs were washed three times in serum-free culture medium (αMEM, 4 mL t = 5 min), before adding serum-free culture medium (2 mL) and returning to cell incubator (24 h) for secretome accumulation. Afterwards, medium was collected, centrifuged (1500 g, 4 ºC) to remove cell debris and placed on ice until analyzed.  LC-MS/MS analysis Samples were processed for proteomic analysis following the single-pot, solid-phase-enhanced sample-preparation (SP3) procedure and enzymatically digested with Trypsin/LysC. Then, samples were analyzed using a nanoLC-MS/MS system composed of a Q Exactive Hybrid Quadrupole-Orbitrap mass spectrometer (Thermo Scientific) coupled to an UltiMate 3000 liquid chromatography system (Dionex). Peptides (500 ng) from each sample were loaded onto a trap cartridge (Acclaim PepMap C18, 100 Å, 5 mm × 0.3 mm, Thermo Scientific) in a mobile phase of 2 % acetonitrile, 0.1 % formic acid at 10 μL/min. After 3 min loading, the trap column was switched in-line to an EASY- Spray column (PepMap RSLC, C18, 2 μm, 50 cm × 75 μm inner diameter, Thermo Scientific) at a flow rate of 250 nL/min. Separation was achieved by mixing mobile phase A (0.1 % formic acid) and B (80 % acetonitrile, 0.1 % formic acid) with the following gradient: 5 min (2.5 to 10 % B), 120 min (10 to 30 % B), 20 min (30 to 50 % B), 5 min (50 to 99 % B), and 10 min (hold 99 % B). Afterwards, the column was equilibrated with solvent B (2.5 %, 17 min). The mass spectrometer was controlled by Xcalibur 4.0 and Tune 2.11 software (Thermo Scientific), operated at 1.9 kV spray voltage in data-dependent positive acquisition mode over a 380-1580 m/z range, alternating with HCD MS/MS of the 10 most intense peaks (normalized collision energy of 27 %). Global settings were as follows: ‘use lock masses’ option set to ‘best’ (m/z 445.12003), ‘lock mass injection’ performed in ‘full MS’ mode, chromatographic peak width set at 15 s. Full scan parameters were set to a resolution of 70 000 (m/z 200), automatic gain control target of 3 × 106 and maximum injection time of 120 ms. Data-dependent settings were as follows: minimum automatic gain control target of 8 × 103; intensity threshold set at 7.3 × 104; ‘Charge exclusion’ set to encompass ‘unassigned’, ‘1’,  ‘8’, and ‘>  8’; ‘Peptide match’ set to ‘preferred’, ‘Exclude isotopes’ set to ‘on’, ‘Dynamic exclusion’ set to ‘45 s’. MS2 settings included: Microscans set to 1, resolution at 35 000 (m/z 200), automatic gain control target of 2 × 105, maximum injection time of 110 ms, isolation window of 2.0 m/z, dynamic first mass and ‘Spectrum data type’ set to ‘Profile’.
pride_data.dataProcessingProtocol: Raw files for the secretome were analyzed in the MaxQuant software (version 2.0.1.0). The initial maximum allowed mass deviation for monoisotopic precursor ions and MS/MS peaks was set to 6 ppm and 20 ppm, respectively. Enzyme specificity was set to trypsin/LysC, defined as C-terminal to arginine and lysine excluding proline, and a maximum of two missed cleavages was allowed. Minimum peptide length of 6 amino acids was set as the threshold. Cysteine Carbamidomethylation was set as a fixed modification, while deamidation, N-terminal acetylation and methionine oxidation were set as variable modification. Spectra were searched by the Andromeda search engine against the human UniProt sequence database (release date 01-2023) with 248 common contaminants and concatenated with the reversed versions of all sequences. The false discovery rate (FDR) was set to 1 % for peptide and protein identifications.
